The {{Nihongo|'''Missionary Office'''|宣教使|senkyōshi}}<ref name="teeuwen-2017a">{{Cite journal |last1=Teeuwen |first1=Mark |last2=Zhong |first2=Yijiang |date=2017 |title=Izumo, Ise, and Modern Shinto |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/90017702 |journal=Japanese Journal of Religious Studies |volume=44 |issue=2 |pages=325–332 |doi=10.18874/jjrs.44.2.2017.325-332 |jstor=90017702 |issn=0304-1042|hdl=10852/65297 |hdl-access=free }}</ref> was one of the government offices in Japan during the Meiji period (1868-1912).<ref>{{Cite web |last=小項目事典,世界大百科事典内言及 |first=日本大百科全書(ニッポニカ),精選版 日本国語大辞典,デジタル大辞泉,ブリタニカ国際大百科事典 |title=宣教使とは |url=https://kotobank.jp/word/%E5%AE%A3%E6%95%99%E4%BD%BF-88095 |access-date=2022-06-26 |website=コトバンク |language=ja}}</ref>

The mission was found to be too socially divisive and the office was abolished in 1872 and replaced with the [[Ministry of Religion (Japan)|Ministry of Religion]], which was presented as neutral between Shinto and Buddhism.<ref name="teeuwen-2017a" />
